name: Chao Nian Gao

ingredients.name: fresh sliced oval Chinese rice cakes

steps: Check the oval rice cakes and mushroom sauce are vegetarian. Separate the fresh rice-cake slices gently with your fingers and rinse briefly; drain well. Cut napa cabbage into bite-size strips and quarter the baby bok choy, washing between its leaves. Slice the shiitake mushrooms, cut carrot into thin matchsticks, chop garlic and cut spring onion into short pieces.

Whisk soy sauce, vegetarian mushroom sauce, sugar, white pepper and sesame oil in a small bowl. Heat 25 ml neutral oil in a wide wok or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes until the mushrooms start to brown; add garlic and the pale parts of spring onion for 30 seconds.

Add napa cabbage and bok choy stems with the remaining 20 ml oil. Stir-fry 2 minutes until slightly softened, then fold in the bok choy leaves. Spread the vegetables into an even bed and place the drained oval rice cakes over them rather than directly on the hot pan, so the cakes do not stick.

Pour the measured 180 ml water around the pan, cover and steam over medium heat for 2–3 minutes. Uncover and gently lift the rice cakes apart with a spatula. They should be soft and chewy, not hard in the middle; if necessary, cover for another 1 minute using the liquid already in the pan.

Pour in the soy-mushroom sauce and stir-fry gently for 1–2 minutes until the liquid reduces to a thin glossy coating on the rice cakes and vegetables. Scatter over the green spring-onion pieces, divide into four warm plates and serve immediately.
tips: These are thin oval Chinese rice-cake slices, distinct from the short cylindrical Korean cakes in Rabokki. Fresh or refrigerated slices need only brief steaming; dried cakes require the soaking instructions on their packet. Use a mushroom-based vegetarian sauce, never oyster sauce.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
